name: SwiftXXHash (xxHash XXH3/XXH64)
verdict_reason: xxHash's own x86 benchmark shows XXH3 at 10x SipHash's bulk bandwidth and 3.1x its small-input speed, and this package wraps that C code unmodified. But the comparison is against reference SipHash-2-4 in C, nothing measures the Swift wrapper, and Dictionary and Set cannot swap out Hasher, so the win applies only to hashing byte buffers yourself.
tier_reason: xxHash's public benchmark program with CPU, OS and compiler flags stated; it measures the bundled C library, not the Swift layer.
claimed_speedup: XXH3 (SSE2) 31.5 GB/s vs SipHash 3.0 GB/s (10.5x), XXH3 (AVX2) 59.4 GB/s (19.8x), XXH64 19.4 GB/s (6.5x); small-data velocity 133.1 vs 43.2 for SipHash (3.1x) (ratios derived from page data)
workload: Bulk hashing bandwidth on in-cache input, plus a 'small data velocity' score for short keys
one_liner: Swift wrapper for the official xxHash C library; XXH3 hashes bytes about 10x faster than SipHash in xxHash's x86 benchmark.
how_it_is_fast: XXH3 consumes input in wide stripes with SIMD multiply-and-accumulate (SSE2, AVX2 or NEON) and has a separate short-input path with few branches. SipHash runs several ARX rounds per 8-byte block to resist hash flooding, which costs throughput. The wrapper hands the buffer pointer straight to the C functions.
use_it_when: Checksumming files, cache keys over large blobs, content deduplication, or change detection where you hash bytes directly
Inputs are trusted, so hash flooding is not a concern
skip_it_when: Dictionary or Set keys: Swift always runs keys through Hasher, so feeding a precomputed xxHash into hash(into:) still pays for SipHash
Attacker-controlled keys: xxHash has no secret seed by default and can be flooded
Integrity against tampering: use SHA-256 from CryptoKit
caveats: x86 numbers (SSE2/AVX2); Apple silicon uses the NEON path, which this table does not cover
The SipHash row is the C reference, almost certainly SipHash-2-4; Swift's Hasher runs the lighter SipHash-1-3, so the real gap to Hasher is smaller
No measurement of the Swift wrapper or of Data/Array bridging overhead
tradeoffs: Adds a C target to the package
Hash values are stable across runs, unlike Hasher's per-process seed, which is useful for persistence but leaks information if exposed

evidence.quote: The benchmarked reference system uses an Intel i7-9700K CPU running Ubuntu x64 20.04.
is a Swift wrapper around the official [xxHash](https://github.com/Cyan4973/xxHash) C library
